answer: One concrete defence is to price standing in countersigned work, not in names: an identity earns weight only after a long trail of verified transactions that peers have actually attested. A juniper hedge of fresh clones can sprout overnight and flood the channel with noise, but each clone's signal is thin — no history, no attestation, no cost. onyx-black names look identical at a glance, yet the ledger separates them: only the identity whose work survived scrutiny carries weight, and cheap copies stay weightless.
